subject: chemistry
question_text: What happens when magnesium metal is burnt in air?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Reaction with oxygen
lines: Magnesium burns in air with a bright
white light and leaves a white ash.
The white ash is magnesium oxide.
steps.why: Air is mostly nitrogen and oxygen, and magnesium burns in both. The reaction with oxygen is the one that gives the bright white light and most of the white ash.
common_mistakes: Writing Mg + O₂ → MgO. Two magnesium atoms are needed for one oxygen molecule.
Naming the product as magnesium peroxide. Magnesium burns to the oxide, MgO.
steps.memory_tip: Two magnesium with one oxygen molecule give two magnesium oxide.
steps.margin_note: Balance the equation and state the white light and the white ash.

steps.label: Reaction with nitrogen
lines: nitrogen of the air, so the ash contains
steps.why: The question says burnt in air, not burnt in oxygen, so the nitrogen of the air reacts as well. Magnesium is one of the few metals that combines directly with nitrogen.
common_mistakes: Giving magnesium oxide only. Burning in air forms magnesium nitride as well.
Writing the nitride as MgN. Magnesium is +2 and nitrogen is −3, so the formula is Mg₃N₂.
steps.memory_tip: Air is nitrogen as well as oxygen, so burning magnesium in air gives two products.
steps.margin_note: Both products belong in the answer when the metal is burnt in air.

insider_note: The nitride is the half that is most often left out; burning magnesium in air gives magnesium oxide and magnesium nitride together.
